messages:
Renee (AE): Heads-up — Prospect Wildflower wants a 5-day POC. They're bringing a custom adapter bundle 'wf-llama-adapt14b-q4k.tar.gz'. Need compat, perf, and security answers before kickoff.
Diego (SE): Do we know tokenizer type? Adapters often assume HuggingFace BPE or custom merges.
Renee (AE): They attached vocab.json + merges.txt in the deal folder and asked specifically about KV cache compatibility and any model artifact signing requirements.
Sana (Solutions Engineer): Short: we can serve q4_k adapters but must validate tokenizer mapping and check whether the adapter injects intermediate states that change KV layout. If adapter only changes weights, KV cache works. If it inserts extra attention gates we might need an adapter shim.
Diego (SE): Running a quick validation locally:
```
redwoodctl validate-model --bundle s3://wildflower/poc/wf-llama-adapt14b.tar.gz --checks tokenizer,kvcache,ops
```
CLI output: "warn: fused_mm_op not available on runtime profile" — fallback to slower kernel. Will try alternative kernel profile.
Martin (Infra): If we switch kernel profile we can route the canary to a dedicated pool with alt kernels. Provisioning + config ~2h. Not a blocker but FYI for scheduling.
Renee (AE): Wildflower expects ~200ms p95 for 512 tokens. Is that realistic for q4_k 14B?
Sana (Solutions Engineer): On an A10/A100 class node with KV cache enabled and single-request mode, 150-190ms p95 is typical. To guarantee 200ms we'd want dedicated nodes and to tune batching and cache TTL.
Renee (AE): Pricing ask: 5-day POC with 2 dedicated nodes + canary + infra support — what's ballpark?
Diego (SE): Ballpark infra: $900/day. We can offer the first 2 days free for sales-led POC. Also include a short perf report and configuration notes.
kms-bot: Security scan results: 3 findings — (1) artifact not signed, (2) missing KMS principal for service account, (3) audit retention default=90d (request=365d).
Claire (Legal): We need to answer their vendor questionnaire. For HSM: hosted won't provide customer HSM; Private deployment can. For KMS: we support customer-managed CMK on Private and can add a dedicated CMK for hosted POC as an exception.
Martin (Infra): KMS policy entry is quick to add for the service principal. Artifact signing requires either their CI to sign the bundle or an exception for POC where we accept unsigned artifacts with a note in the security response.
Diego (SE): Follow-up on compat: after testing with runtime flag `--enable-alt-kernels` tokenizer and KV cache checks passed. Perf baseline locally ~165ms p95 single-shot with KV cache warm. Will run dedicated canary tomorrow AM.
Sana (Solutions Engineer): Action items: (1) Diego to run canary on dedicated pool and post perf logs; (2) Martin to provision short-lived dedicated pool and add KMS policy entry; (3) Claire to draft questionnaire responses and highlight HSM/private requirement; (4) Renee to confirm POC schedule and pricing with customer.
Renee (AE): I'll propose Tue kickoff and note the complimentary 2-day window. Will call out HSM constraint and need for artifact signing.
Diego (SE): I'll post `redwoodctl validate` logs in the ticket after canary. If we hit any op-level mismatches I'll open infra PR.
Claire (Legal): I'll draft replies and put them in the deal folder by EOD. If Wildflower insists on HSM for hosted, escalate to sales ops for Private pricing.
Martin (Infra): Starting infra ticket now and will attach runbook.
Renee (AE): Thanks all — please ping here when canary passes. Closing thread for now. :white_check_mark:
